name: Toyota
overview: Australia's perpetual market leader and automotive titan. Toyota began Australian operations in 1958 with LandCruisers on the Snowy Mountains Scheme and assembled vehicles locally at Port Melbourne and Altona from 1963 to 2017.
australian_history:
Toyota's Australian story began in 1958 when civil engineering contractor Leslie Thiess imported 13 FJ25 LandCruisers for use on the rugged construction terrain of the Snowy Mountains Hydro-Electric Scheme. Impressed by their unbreakable mechanical toughness, Thiess secured Queensland distribution rights in 1959, forming Thiess Toyota.

In 1963, Australian Motor Industries (AMI) at Port Melbourne, Victoria negotiated CKD (Complete Knock Down) assembly rights for Toyota passenger cars, making Australia Toyota's very first vehicle manufacturing site outside of Japan. The first vehicle assembled was the Tiara (RT20/RT30), quickly followed by the Corona in 1964, the Crown luxury sedan, and the Corolla (KE10) in 1968.

By the 1970s, Toyota had expanded into full Australian manufacturing. Toyota Motor Corporation Japan gradually acquired shares in AMI, renaming the operation Toyota Motor Corporation Australia (TMCA). Under the Federal Government's Button Car Plan in 1989, Toyota and General Motors-Holden established the United Australian Automotive Industries (UAAI) joint venture. Holden built the Commodore for Toyota to sell as the Toyota Lexcen, while Toyota manufactured the Corolla and Camry for Holden to sell as the Holden Nova and Apollo.

In 1994, Toyota commissioned a brand new, world-class vehicle manufacturing complex at Altona in Melbourne's western suburbs, transitioning Port Melbourne to engine manufacturing and casting. In 2000, Toyota introduced the Altona-built Avalon large sedan, later replaced in 2006 by the 3.5L V6 Aurion alongside the Camry. In 2010, Altona launched Australia's very first locally manufactured hybrid passenger car, the Camry Hybrid (AHV40), unveiled by Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

Toyota officially overtook Holden and Ford in 2003 to become Australia's overall best-selling automotive brand, a crown it has held without interruption for over two decades. The HiLux utility and RAV4 crossover have repeatedly been Australia's #1 selling individual vehicles. Local car assembly concluded at Altona on October 3, 2017 after 54 years and 3,451,115 vehicles built. Toyota maintains its Australian headquarters, national engineering center, product design studio, and extensive testing grounds at Altona and Anglesea.

models.name: Camry
models.overview: The Toyota Camry was the cornerstone of Australian automotive manufacturing from 1987 to 2017. Built in Port Melbourne and Altona, it was Australia's favourite mid-size family and fleet sedan for over three decades.

models.name: Corolla
models.overview: The Toyota Corolla is the world's most produced passenger car and an integral part of Australian life. Assembled locally in Victoria for over 30 years (1968-1999), it has provided dependable motoring for generations of Australians.

models.name: Crown
models.overview: The Toyota Crown established Toyota's reputation for engineering refinement and reliability in Australia. Built locally from CKD packs by Australian Motor Industries (AMI) in Port Melbourne from 1967 to 1979, the Crown offered six-cylinder prestige, luxurious appointments, and long-legged durability across five distinct Australian generations.

models.name: Aurion
models.overview: The Toyota Aurion was an Australian-manufactured large front-wheel-drive sedan engineered to compete directly against the Holden Commodore and Ford Falcon. Powered exclusively by the 200kW 3.5-litre 2GR-FE V6 and built at Altona, Victoria, it also sired the legendary Eaton TVS supercharged 241kW TRD Aurion.

models.name: Tiara
models.overview: The first Toyota assembled in Australia by AMI in Port Melbourne, laying the foundation for Toyota's domestic manufacturing history.

models.name: Corona
models.overview: Long-running Australian family car assembled in Port Melbourne across multiple generations until succeeded by the Camry.

models.name: Avalon
models.overview: Spacious family and taxi sedan built at Altona to take on Holden Commodore and Ford Falcon.

models.name: Lexcen
models.overview: Holden Commodore rebadged as a Toyota under the Button Plan joint venture (UAAI), built at Holden's Elizabeth plant.

models.name: Celica
models.overview: The Toyota Celica was Australia's definitive Japanese sports coupe for 34 years across seven generations. From the Mustang-inspired TA22 and RA28 liftbacks of the 1970s to the championship-winning turbo all-wheel-drive GT-Four rally homologation specials and high-revving 2ZZ-GE VVTL-i ZR, the Celica defined stylish sports performance.

models.name: LandCruiser
models.overview: The LandCruiser is the undisputed King of the Australian Outback. First brought to Australia in 1958 for the Snowy Mountains Scheme, it has conquered the country's most unforgiving deserts, pastoral stations, and mines for nearly seven decades.

models.name: HiLux
models.overview: The Toyota HiLux is an Australian cultural icon and the country's best-selling vehicle outright from 2016 through 2022. Renowned for near-indestructible durability, it serves on construction sites, farms, mining operations, and outback tracks nationwide.

models.name: HiAce
models.overview: The Toyota HiAce is the unquestioned titan of Australian commercial vans and passenger shuttle transport. Across more than half a century, its cab-over and semi-bonnet configurations have kept Australian tradespeople, couriers, airport shuttles, and tourism fleets moving with renowned reliability and outstanding resale value.

models.name: LandCruiser Prado
models.overview: The Toyota LandCruiser Prado is Australia's perennial favorite family and long-distance outback touring 4WD. Bridging the gap between the mid-size RAV4 and heavy-duty LandCruiser wagon, the Prado delivers genuine off-road capability, dual long-range fuel tanks, up to seven seats, and legendary durability.

models.name: Supra
models.overview: The Toyota Supra is a halo sports grand tourer with an indelible legacy in Australian motorsport and enthusiast culture. From early Celica Supra models through the twin-turbo 2JZ-GTE JZA80 supercar killer to the modern B58-powered GR Supra, it represents Toyota's front-engine rear-drive inline-six performance pinnacle.

models.name: Echo / Yaris / GR Yaris
models.overview: Toyota's light car family in Australia spans from the quirky, spacious Echo through three generations of Yaris hatchbacks and sedans to the hyper-capable GR Yaris Rallye AWD homologation special. Combining exceptional reliability, hybrid fuel efficiency, and World Rally Championship engineering, it is a giant of small-car motoring.

models.name: Kluger
models.overview: The Toyota Kluger (sold globally as the Highlander) is Australia's quintessential car-based 7-seat family crossover SUV. Blending passenger-car ride comfort with cavernous interior room, powerful V6 and hybrid powertrains, and all-weather AWD assurance, it became a cornerstone of Australian suburban family motoring.

models.name: RAV4
models.overview: The Toyota RAV4 created the compact car-based recreational SUV category in 1994. Across five generations, it grew into Australia's favourite SUV, with the XA50 Hybrid triggering unprecedented multi-month waitlists.

models.name: 86 / GR86
models.overview: The Toyota 86 and GR86 re-energized accessible rear-wheel-drive sports motoring in Australia. Developed jointly with Subaru (who built the cars at the Gunma Main Plant), the 86 combined a low center of gravity boxer engine, lightweight chassis, razor-sharp steering, and rear-drive dynamics at an accessible price point.

models.name: MR2

Built locally from CKD packs by Australian Motor Industries (AMI) in Port Melbourne from 1967 to 1979, the Crown offered six-cylinder prestige, luxurious appointments, and long-legged durability across five distinct Australian generations.
crown.australian_market_notes: First imported in 1964, local assembly at AMI's Port Melbourne plant began with the MS55 third generation in 1967. aurion.australian_market_notes: Conceived specifically for the Australian market and regional export, the Aurion was launched in October 2006. The TRD Aurion 3500S and 3500SL, developed by Toyota Racing Development Australia and Prodrive at Clayton VIC, became the world's most powerful front-wheel drive production sedan at release. Production ended on 3 October 2017 with the closure of Altona manufacturing.

celica.overview: The Toyota Celica was Australia's definitive Japanese sports coupe for 34 years across seven generations. celica.australian_market_notes: Introduced to Australia in 1971 by Thiess Toyota and AMI, the Celica won immense praise for pairing affordable coupe styling with bulletproof mechanicals.
